W B 78 for oboe, 2 horns, violin, cello, keyboard; three recordings run 14:08-17:01. 1785 is the Luther print year (composition undated). The print says harpsichord only; the house piano rule for post-1770 prints might apply, as for the other Op. 22 entries

IMSLP lists No. 6 (B-flat) as Andante + Menuetto; Coviello plays that B-flat quartet as Andante 10:05 + Minuetto 5:55 = 16 min under its own numbering. The Nuovo Quartetto Italiano track labelled Op. 8 No. 6 (Allegro, Rondo) is probably W B 60
Camerata Köln (CPO 1998) plays it 6:22+5:03+3:39 = 15 min; three movements as stated
Op. 19 No. 2 is the quartet printed for flute and oboe (or two flutes), tenor and cello (Amadeus edition lists oboe (violin)); CPO 14:44
CPO timings 6:31+2:51+3:12 = 12:34, three movements as stated
Two flutes, violin, cello (the only Op. 19 quartet with violin); CPO 15:57
Op. 2 No. 5 (W B 47), Trio 1790 plays Vivace 4:14 + Tempo di menuetto 3:05 = 7 min
Op. 2 No. 6 (W B 48), Trio 1790 plays Allegro moderato 4:53 + Rondeau 1:59 = 7 min
1778 is the Hummel (Amsterdam) print; IMSLP's 1762 is only the start of the span '1762-78' (Bach's London years), not a date for this trio. Trio 1790: 5:32+4:23 = 10 min
Op. 15 No. 2 (W B 50); Trio 1790: Allegro 4:51 + Rondo 4:01 = 9 min. 1778 = Hummel print (IMSLP's 1762 is the start of a 1762-78 span)

Wikipedia lists W B 42 as 'Trio for 2 violins & cello in B-flat'; Perlman, Zukerman, Eddy and Sanders (harpsichord) record it (Warner). Bach Digital (via search) dates it c. 1777, from the Bach-Abel-Kammel collection. Cello is the bass line, so the owner may prefer continuo
Oboe quartet W B 60 (Allegro, Rondo); Il Gardellino 10:13, Perlman/Still/Zukerman/Harrell on Warner. Sieber printed it as Op. 14/1; year could be c. 1776 (Bach Digital, via search)
Fortepiano, violin, viola; London Baroque 15:54, Camerata Köln 15:11 (as F. VII/5)
Flute (or violin), cello, concertante harpsichord; Camerata Köln (CPO) 6:20+4:40+4:07 = 15 min as 'HW VII/4, BR B29'
London Baroque (harmonia mundi 2008) plays it as 'two violins and continuo in A major, F. VII/2', 4:45+4:16+2:54 = 12 min; no second recording found
MusicBrainz lists it as BR-JCFB B 12 = Wf VII/3, two violins and continuo (London Baroque 3:46+3:31+2:48 = 10 min). BR B 12 could be added to the title
London Baroque plays it as 'violin, viola and fortepiano in A major, F. VII/6', 7:23+4:15+4:03 = 16 min; no second source found
Nimbus: 15:35, played on two flutes + harpsichord; IMSLP scoring is flute, violin, keyboard. The violin-to-flute alternative rests on that recording only; 1770-80 per the review
Vox Luminis/Clematis (Ricercar, 2026) 7:21; IMSLP: violin, 2 violas, continuo (the third RISM viola is the bass)
Wikipedia: 'doubtful, possibly by C. P. E. Bach'; four movements; three recordings run 7:16-8:31 min
Single canonic movement for oboe, violin, continuo, under two minutes; also used in Cantatas 208 and 68. Ensemble La Selva records it alone (1:23)
Hänssler 2022: 7:58+17:18+6:36 = 32 min; variations on the Volga song are the slow movement
Rampal/Zukerman (Sony) 13:40, Nimbus 20:16 (minutes 14 follows Sony); review says more likely by W. Friedemann Bach but published as W. F. E.'s, as the note states
Eybler Quartet with Jane Booth (Analekta 2010): 8:49+3:18+8:51 = 21 min. UNC catalogue dates it c. 1828-30 (uncertain); published by Kneusslin, Peters edition
Year 1992 (Montrose Trio programme notes: five-movement suite reusing two movements of Roots, 1978). Friedberg album 25:37 and Montrose Trio concert 2022 pass the floor
Oregon String Quartet (Koch/eOne 2006): 8:28+7:42+5:06+9:34 = 31 min, four movements; LKM/Hal Leonard edition; composition year not found
Print has optional horns only in Nos. 1, 2 and 4, so 'no horns' holds for No. 3; Le Concerto Rococo 5:14+4:04+2:48 = 12 min; print says clavecin ou forte-piano
Fretwork, In Nomine II (Signum 2019) lists John Baldwin 'Proportions to the Minim' 2:31; IMSLP: Commonplace Book, 4 viols
Le Musiche da Camera (Tactus 2013): 6:22+1:44+2:19 = 10 min, three movements. IMSLP scoring 'cello/continuo'; printed for two violins and cello

Sonata terza (Amoroso, Allegro, Adagio, Allegro; 10:28 on the Bergamo CD) is also recorded by Musica Antiqua Köln/Heyens ('Vivaldi, Mancini & Barbella: Flute Concertos'); IMSLP: recorder, 2 violins, continuo (MS parts add a violetta)
Wikipedia: Serenade Op. 1 (1928) for string quartet, arranged for string orchestra 1944; Endellion 9:41, Ying 8:33

Scoring unresolved: IMSLP tags it 2 cellos + continuo (Grove: cello duet) and says the print names no instrument for the treble-clef top line. Both recordings (Cocset/Les Basses Réunies 8:39; TIEFSAITS 'A TRE', 3 cellos, 7:59) play it on cellos; 'violin or pardessus de viole' is an inference. Exists and is recorded; consider cello 2 + continuo, or drop as unspecified top instrument
